title: Augmentation height equals global dimension
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite type commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] equipped with a commutative Hopf algebra structure. Explicitly, it has a coassociative $k$-algebra coproduct $\Delta:A\to A\otimes_k A$, a $k$-algebra counit $\varepsilon:A\to k$ with $(\varepsilon\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta=\mathrm{id}$ under the tensor unit identifications, and a $k$-linear antipode $S$ such that $\mu(S\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta=\mu(\mathrm{id}\otimes S)\Delta=u\varepsilon$, where $\mu$ is multiplication and $u:k\to A$ the structure map [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Then $\operatorname{ht}(\ker\varepsilon)=\dim A$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. No characteristic or reducedness assumption is made.

proof.text: For algebraically closed k, every maximal ideal of A is ker(g) for a k-algebra point g:A→k by the weak Nullstellensatz. Convolution translation by g is an algebra automorphism with inverse translation by the convolution inverse of g. The counit identities show that translation sends the identity point to g, so ker(g) and ker(ε) have equal heights. This does not use reducedness.

source.place: Proof, Dimension paragraph: translations identify local dimensions and the dimension is their maximum

proof.text: The counit onto k ensures A≠0. The Krull dimension is the supremum of maximal-ideal heights: extend any finite prime chain to a maximal ideal. All maximal-ideal heights from the first step are the height of ker ε. Hence dim A=ht ker ε over an algebraically closed field.

source.place: Proof, Dimension paragraph: translations identify local dimensions and the dimension is their maximum

proof.text: For arbitrary k put K=algebraic closure(k) and B=K⊗_k A. The base-changed counit sends λ⊗a to λ ε(a). The inclusion A→B is faithfully flat and integral: K/k is algebraic, and base change preserves integrality. Incomparability bounds dim B≤dim A, while surjectivity on prime spectra and going-down lift each chain and give the reverse bound. Thus dim B=dim A.

source.place: Proof, Dimension paragraph: translations identify local dimensions and the dimension is their maximum

proof.text: Let p=ker ε and P=ker ε_K. The equality P∩A=p follows by evaluating the inclusion. Tensoring A/p=k shows B/pB=K, and P maps to the zero ideal of this quotient. Both A and B are Noetherian, since they are finite type over fields. The flat height formula gives ht P=ht p+0. Apply the algebraically closed case to B and combine this with dim B=dim A.

mathlib_searches.query: The height of the augmentation ideal of a finite type commutative Hopf algebra equals its Krull dimension
For a finite type commutative Hopf algebra over any field, the height of the augmentation ideal equals the global Krull dimension

lean.statement: theorem height_ker_counit_eq_ringKrullDim (k A : Type*) [Field k] [CommRing A] [HopfAlgebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] : ((RingHom.ker (Bialgebra.counitAlgHom k A)).height : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim A
